subject: Post-demo: deployment preference & migration options — next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finsearch.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment preference & migration options — next steps

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Recap (minutes):
- FinSearch main goals: low tail latency for ingestion pipelines, predictable unit cost for batch embeddings, and strict data isolation for PII workloads.
- Migration sources discussed: (a) OpenAI-hosted APIs, (b) self-hosted models running on your K8s/VM fleet, (c) legacy GPU cluster running a mix of PyTorch endpoints.
- Top-of-mind constraint: SOC 2/audit evidence for dedicated environments and encryption in transit + at rest.

Decision points we need from you (short answers are fine):
1) Preferred deployment mode: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on-prem).
2) Migration priority: move traffic off OpenAI first, or consolidate self-hosted / legacy clusters first?
3) Any non-negotiable compliance elements (e.g., no egress outside your VPC, specific KMS requirement)?

What I recommend based on today: Dedicated capacity as a first step (predictable throughput and data isolation) with an optional Private/VPC lift for regulated workloads later. Dedicated lets us do a faster canary and keep production SLAs while we validate model parity.

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm your preferred deployment mode and migration priority by EOD Thursday.
- I attached a short deployment-decision-checklist and a migration-assessment-template — please fill the highlighted fields where possible.
- If Dedicated looks right, we can schedule a 30-min tech-ops call (aditya + vivek) to review network topology and data flows.

Attachments: deployment-decision-checklist.xlsx; migration-assessment-template.docx

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0189

--
On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 13:00 Liam O'Connor <liam@finsearch.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the walkthrough today. The latency numbers looked promising.
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finsearch.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment preference & migration options — next steps

Hi Stephanie —

Great recap, thanks. A few quick answers and follow-ups from our side: 

1) Deployment preference: We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity. Primary reasons: predictable throughput for our nightly indexing jobs and ability to isolate PII workloads.
2) Migration priority: We'd prefer to migrate the legacy GPU cluster first (the cluster is older, less maintainable) and keep the OpenAI traffic while we validate model parity.
3) Compliance: We need proof of key management options (KMS/HSM) and we cannot have egress from regulated subnets to public endpoints. Can your Dedicated offering be placed inside a customer VPC or peered privately?

Also, can you share an estimate for how long the cluster migration typically takes and an initial ballpark for committed capacity pricing? Happy to hop on a short call with your engineers.

Thanks —
Liam O'Connor
Head of ML Platform | FinSearch Analytics
liam@finsearch.ai
+1 (617) 555-0222

Subject: Fwd: FinSearch - Dedicated preference + questions

Forwarding FinSearch responses — they want Dedicated, and they want us to confirm KMS/HSM options and private peering for egress control. They also asked for a timeline and committed capacity ballpark.

Action items I propose: 
- Aditya: validate migration effort from legacy GPU cluster -> Redwood Dedicated; call out model format compatibility (PT checkpoints, Triton endpoints, GGML if present) and typical blockers.
- Vivek: draft a committed-capacity estimate (3 sizing scenarios: small/medium/large) with expected cost per 1M tokens and latency SLOs. Include option for a VPC peering/private endpoint.
- I will own a 30-min technical alignment call with FinSearch; propose Thu 10am PT or Fri 9am PT.

Please reply with brief confirmations and any questions. I attached an internal MVP-migration-checklist for you to annotate.

Thanks —
Stephanie
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@finsearch.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinSearch - Dedicated preference + questions

Stephanie / Vivek / Liam —

I can take point on the migration feasibility check. Preliminary notes after skimming the checklist: 
- Model formats: If the legacy cluster serves PyTorch checkpoints via a custom Flask endpoint, we typically need to export to a supported serialized format (TorchScript/ONNX) and validate optimized kernels. If you're serving via Triton, migration is usually straightforward.
- KV cache & state: We'll need to confirm how session affinity is handled today; long-running KV state across tokens will affect our batching strategy.
- Estimated lift: 4–8 weeks for a minimal migration (sanity checks, staging canary, metrics parity). Larger if you require custom ops or in-house plugins.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS in both AWS and GCP regions; we can provide certificate of attestation and architecture diagram for private peering.

Next immediate step: I can run a short tech call (30m) to map current endpoints and a plan for export/validation. Liam — which time between Thu 10am PT / Fri 9am PT works?

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.inference

Look forward to the call.

Liam
